svg.title: Overview: a per-state perturbation probe under open-loop replay and closed-loop replanning, fitted over a finite window and gated into stable, deadband, or unstable; the labels show state-dependent rates, a horizon effect, rare contraction under replanning, and partial predictability from observation.
svg.text: What happens to an action error after it enters the system?
12 tasks · robomimic, MimicGen, RoboCasa · diffusion policies and GR00T N1.5

g.text: Perturb one action at a state
Add δ to the translation of the first action,
scaled to the policy's own action error σu.
Demonstration → rollout changes the state distribution;
rollout → policy chunk changes the action source.
The same perturbed start, followed two ways.
Recorded actions replayed unchanged; no policy queried.
Measures what the plant and task geometry do with the error.
Policy replans at every step after the perturbation.
Paired branches share policy randomness (common random numbers).
A rate over a finite window K
Fit the log state deviation against steps j:
λ̄ and its standard error over N branches.
K is a property of the measurement, not of the chunk:
24 steps for most stamps, 8 for the emitted policy chunks.
Large enough to matter, and resolved from zero.
an m-fold change over the window (m = 2)
Both pass → stable if λ̄ < 0, unstable if λ̄ > 0.
Either fails → deadband: a statement about
resolution, not a claim that the rate is zero.
No single rate describes a task
One trajectory, one label per state (illustrative).
Confident contraction is rare; amplification is
common among states whose rate is resolved.
Rates vary within a task, so one global
The fitting window changes the answer
Divergence is front-loaded: a fast rise,
then a plateau. A short window fits the rise.
21.1% at K = 24 → 69.7% at K = 8; stable stays 0.0%.
λ summarizes an interval, not a time-invariant rate.
confidently stable under replanning; they move to
the deadband or stay unstable, on all three suites.
Open loop is visible; closed loop only partly
The open-loop regime can be ranked from
what the robot sees. The closed-loop rate is
only partly recoverable: it also depends on
how the policy acts after the perturbation.
Adding the action chunk improves rate regression
and rank correlation, as expected when the target
depends on the particular sequence replayed.

svg.text: Labels at m = 2.0, t = 2.365. Demonstration, rollout, and closed-loop stamps are fitted over K = 24; policy chunks over the emitted chunk length (8 for the diffusion policies, up to 24 on RoboCasa).
